target_customer: Consumers ordering food delivery, monetized through affiliate fees from delivery platforms
problem: Delivery apps make users choose a platform, then a restaurant, then a dish, and review data is thin at the dish level.
business_model: Affiliate revenue from delivery orders placed through a dish-level review app

founders.name: Richard Wu
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Later Director of Product at Woflow; Simmer was an early Woflow customer per a search summary.

founders.name: Vaibhav Verma
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives a shared note for both founders, so individual employers are not separately confirmed.

exit.reason: Founders decided to close after the pandemic began, about two years in, as described by Richard Wu on a Pilot blog.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a custom sentiment analyzer to aggregate dish mentions from blogs, social media and newspapers into per-dish ratings, which is standard NLP work with data cleaning challenges for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: The aggregated dish rating index could accumulate, but the underlying data is public and delivery platforms or Yelp could build similar ratings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Simmer. The founder describes a chicken and egg problem getting dish reviews and users.

market_need_then: The YC description argues delivery apps are bad experiences with too many choices. A founder interview says the team was trying to build Yelp for dishes and claimed 380k ratings across about 5k restaurants in San Francisco, Manhattan and Chicago.

branding.domain_note: Product site was usesimmer.com per a directory listing, not simmer.com.

rebrands.why: Product Hunt lists the product as Simmer (formerly Foodie); no reason or date found.

brand_strength.rationale: Only Product Hunt listings and directories mention the brand. Many unrelated products share the name Simmer, which hurts search and recall.

outcome_analysis: Simmer tried to build a Yelp for dishes by aggregating public reviews and earning affiliate fees, and the founder says it faced a chicken and egg problem needing dish reviews to attract users. After about two years and as the pandemic began, the founders chose to close the company in 2020. The cause beyond that account is thin, and the affiliate model depended on delivery platforms.
notes: No company website listed on YC; usesimmer.com was not opened, treat the site as dead or unverified. Funding is conflicting across databases: Village lists $150K total with last round seed, StartupBlink lists $300K, Seedtable lists none. Amounts are therefore not recorded and the seed round rests on a single database. A CB Insights entry marked Alive appears to be a different Simmer. Failory says Summer 2019 while YC says Winter 2019; YC used. Competitors left empty because only undated Product Hunt and SaaSHub alternatives pages were found. Exit date 2020 is approximate from the founder account.
